Chapter 9: Sustaining Practice—Building Habits for Lasting Change
Let’s be honest—lasting change doesn’t come from one big aha moment. It’s all about steady, repeated practice. Our brains are wired for change, thanks to something called plasticity. So, every little effort you make really does matter. Small steps, taken again and again, can actually reshape how you think and live.
But let’s face it, keeping up with any new habit—especially when life gets hectic or you hit a rough patch—can be tough. Here’s an image that might help: think of your new habit like tending a campfire. At first, the flames are tiny, needing your constant care and attention. With a little fuel—maybe a moment of mindfulness, a bit of gratitude, or a simple act of kindness—your fire gets stronger, warmer, and much easier to keep burning.
So, what can you do to keep your practice alive, even on those busy or challenging days? Here are a few strategies that really work:
First, set realistic intentions. Don’t try to change everything at once. Pick just one or two practices to focus on. It’s a lot more doable, and you’ll see progress faster.
Second, create reminders. Use whatever cues you can—a sticky note on your mirror, a gentle alarm on your phone, or even a favorite object in your pocket—to nudge yourself back to mindful attention throughout the day.
And don’t forget to celebrate the small wins. Every step forward, no matter how tiny, deserves a little recognition. Give yourself credit for showing up and making the effort.
Now, here’s something to pay attention to: setbacks are totally normal. Old habits may pop back up, or your motivation might dip. When that happens, the most important thing is to return to your practice with patience and a bit of self-compassion. Remember, personal growth isn’t a sprint—it’s a lifelong journey.
Over time, these habits won’t feel like chores. They’ll become woven into your everyday life, quietly building your resilience, joy, and wisdom—sometimes in the smallest, most unexpected moments.
